language.script_notes: A Baltic language with the letters ė, š, ž, č, ą, ę, į, ų and ū, and words that commonly end in -as, -is, -ai or -us. The letter ė and the ogonek marks (ą, ę, į, ų) are quick separators from Latvian and Polish.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Wedge-style bollards with orange rectangular reflectors on the front and white ones on the back.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Wedge-shaped post, similar to many others in Europe.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Concrete utility poles carry insulator bulbs in a 1×1, 2×2 or 3×3 arrangement, sometimes an odd number, but not alternating from side to side as in the neighbouring country. Warning signs have a thin red border with a thin white outline.

architecture.roof_style: Steeply pitched roofs on timber and brick houses; flat roofs on Soviet blocks; Baroque towers and domes in the capital.
architecture.wall_construction: Timber and brick village houses; grey Soviet panel blocks; Baroque and Gothic brick churches and a large baroque old town in the capital.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Painted timber, red brick and pastel Baroque plaster.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Roadside wooden crosses and carved shrines; brick Gothic and Baroque churches; white stork nests on utility poles and roofs; Soviet blocks and monuments.

nature.vegetation: Pine and mixed forest, farmland and meadows, many lakes; sandy dunes and pine forest on the Baltic coast.
nature.terrain: Low, flat to gently rolling land with the highest hills only around 300m, and a coast that includes the Curonian Spit's shifting sand dunes.
nature.climate_signature: Cool, damp and often overcast, with long winters.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and a blue EU strip on the left carrying 'LT'.
vehicles.plate_format: Three letters followed by three digits with no space (e.g. 'ABC123').

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of roads and towns.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring Baltic language family, flat landscape and similar villages
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Lithuanian wedge bollards with orange reflectors and non-alternating pole bulbs differ from Latvia's thin white bollards and alternating bulbs; the letter ė and endings like -ai and -as appear here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared border region, Catholic roadside shrines and similar farmland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Polish red-striped bollards and diacritics (ł, ż) differ from Lithuanian ė, š and ogonek letters.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat forest and farmland, Soviet blocks
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Latin script with ė and Lithuanian plates versus Belarusian Cyrillic or Estonia's Õ.
